examples.en: Lunch at work is at twelve.
At lunchtime I take a walk near the office.
Restaurants are crowded at lunchtime.
Lunch break is over. Back to work.
How about a cup of coffee during lunch?

explain: 한국 회사에서는 점심시간에 동료들과 같이 밥을 먹고 커피를 마시는 일이 많아요. ‘점심’과 ‘시간’을 붙여 한 단어로 써요.

dict_examples.en: He met a friend during his lunch break.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.ko: 점심시간이 막 끝난 때여서 다방은 한산했다.
dict_examples.en: It was just after lunchtime ended, so the tearoom was quiet.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: At Korean offices, coworkers often eat lunch together and then have coffee. 점심시간 is written as one word.

examples.en: I'm busy preparing for an exam these days.
My husband takes care of dinner preparation.
Is your bag packed? — Yes, shall we go?
I'm preparing for tomorrow's meeting.
Have you finished preparing for the trip?

explain: ‘저녁을 준비해요’처럼 만들 것을 말하기도 하고, ‘시험 준비를 해요’처럼 앞으로 있을 일을 말하기도 해요. 다 끝났으면 ‘준비됐어요’라고 해요. 학교나 여행에 챙겨 가는 물건은 ‘준비물’이라고 해요.

phrases.en: I am preparing for tomorrow's exam.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding -해요 to 준비 makes it a verb.
Use it when everything is ready.

phrases.en: What do I need to bring tomorrow?
phrases.nuance_en: Things you bring to school or on a trip.

dict_examples.ko: 그녀는 손님을 맞이할 만반의 준비를 끝냈다.
dict_examples.en: She finished every preparation for welcoming the guests.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.ko: 그는 1년 정도의 준비 기간을 거친 뒤 사업을 시작했다.
dict_examples.en: He started his business after about a year of preparation.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.en: Mother is busy preparing for her son's wedding.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.ko: 준비가 부족해서 그들은 여행하는 데 많은 불편을 겪었다.
dict_examples.en: They weren't well prepared, so they had a lot of trouble on their trip.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.en: It was a big exam, so I mentally prepared myself.

explain_en: You can name what you're making, as in ‘저녁을 준비해요’ (I'm preparing dinner), or the upcoming event, as in ‘시험 준비를 해요’ (I'm preparing for an exam). When you're done, say ‘준비됐어요’ (I'm ready). Things you need to bring to school or on a trip are called ‘준비물’.

examples.ko: 오늘 아침에 친구한테서 반가운 소식을 들었어요.
examples.en: This morning I got some good news from a friend.

examples.ko: 요즘 그 친구 소식을 못 들었어요.
examples.en: I haven't heard from that friend lately.
Good news came from my hometown.

examples.ko: 그 가게가 문을 닫았다는 소식을 들었어요.
examples.en: I heard the news that the shop closed down.
I haven't heard anything from my friend who went to Korea.

explain: 소식은 친구나 가족처럼 아는 사람의 이야기에도 써요. 방송이나 신문의 큰 이야기는 보통 “뉴스”라고 해요.
explain_en: 소식 can be news about people you know, like friends and family. Big stories in the media are usually called 뉴스.

dis.h: news or word about someone's situation

p.n: 뉴스 means a media news report, so 'a friend's news' does not fit.

examples.ko: 다음 달에는 복습 횟수를 늘릴 거예요.
examples.en: Next month I'm going to review more often.

examples.ko: 손님이 많아져서 직원을 두 명 늘렸어요.
examples.en: We got busier, so we took on two more staff.

examples.ko: 살을 빼려고 운동 시간을 삼십 분 늘렸어요.
examples.en: To lose weight, I extended my exercise time by thirty minutes.
We increased the café menu to ten items.

examples.ko: 그 식당은 주차 공간을 열 대 더 늘렸어요.
examples.en: That restaurant added ten more parking spaces.

explain: 늘리다의 반대말은 ‘줄이다’예요. ‘늘다/줄다’는 저절로 되는 일이고, ‘늘리다/줄이다’는 사람이 일부러 하는 일이에요.

dict_examples.en: To increase the number of students.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.ko: 그 배역을 맡기 위해 체중을 30kg이나 늘렸다.
dict_examples.en: He gained as much as 30 kg to take on that role.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: The opposite of 늘리다 is 줄이다. 늘다/줄다 happen by themselves, while 늘리다/줄이다 are things a person does on purpose.

examples.en: I slice the onion thinly.
Be careful when you slice vegetables with a knife.
Slice the kimchi first and then stir-fry it.
Slice the green onion into small rounds and put it in the soup.
I sliced the fruit to put it on a plate.
Shall I cut the watermelon in half for you?

explain: '자르다'는 머리카락이나 종이에도 쓰지만 '썰다'는 주로 칼로 음식 재료를 자를 때 써요. 'ㄹ'이 빠져서 '써는', '썬', '썹니다'로 바뀌어요. 아주 잘게 하는 것은 '다지다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: I put the sliced onion on a plate.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이미 썬 재료를 말할 때 '썬'으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 'sseon' for ingredients that are already sliced.

phrases.en: Please don't chop the green onion yet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 하지 말라고 부탁하거나 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to ask someone not to chop yet.

explain_en: '자르다' also works for hair or paper, but '썰다' is mainly for cutting food ingredients with a knife. The 'ㄹ' drops in forms like '써는', '썬' and '썹니다'. Chopping very finely is '다지다'.
